text:
marta: Heads up — after the latest redwoodctl MSI install on Win10, Windows Credential Manager seems to be stashing a stale profile token. Local testing gets stuck in an auth loop when I switch profiles. Anyone seen this?

kevin: Yep, ran into something similar on my dev VM. CredMan shows a single entry named `Redwood CLI` for multiple profiles, so it looks like values are being overwritten/merged.

sam: Workaround that helped me: `redwoodctl login --profile test --force` then `redwoodctl config set profile.test.cache false`. Ugly but stops the immediate loop.

marta: That doesn't persist for me — after reboot local-serve still picks up the cached creds and asks to re-auth. Repro steps I used:
1) fresh MSI install
2) `redwoodctl login` (profile: default)
3) `redwoodctl profiles add --name test --alias ci-test`
4) `redwoodctl local-serve --profile ci-test`
=> CLI prints `Authentication required` and opens browser, then immediately prints `token mismatch` when browser returns.

jen: Could be a dup of an older issue around cred helper precedence. @eng-ml / @eng-infra — is the Windows credential helper emitting a key that includes the profile name?

kevin: I looked at `credential-helper-windows.go` quickly — code is using a static target string `redwoodctl` when calling CredMan. So different profiles end up colliding. I can open a PR to append `:profile=<profile>` to the target.

devex-bot: Issue created: #4583 — "Windows cred helper: include profile in target name" assigned to @kevin. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

sam: :thumbsup: Short-term ops note: you can delete the stale entry from Windows Credential Manager (Control Panel > Credential Manager > Windows Credentials > remove "Redwood CLI") then run `redwoodctl login --profile <name> --force`. We'll add a troubleshooting item to the CLI install docs.

marta: Thanks — will try the delete workaround and report back. If the PR lands we should add an automated test covering multi-profile on Windows so this doesn't regress.
